title: Looking for Tipps for Asset  / Img Gen
author: Accomplished-Cat5451
selftext:
Hey everyone, I've tried using several different models and platforms to generate asset images with a consistent style. I'm using a master prompt, negative prompts, and reference images, but the assets still end up slightly off. I don't know if I've just been staring at them for too long and lost my perspective, or if I'm doing something wrong. Any advice?

  
Prompts i used for the Cliff Trerrain : Use the provided reference image as a strict visual style guide.



Create a MODULAR CLIFF TERRAIN BLOCK as a single isolated game asset belonging to the same unified stylized asset library.



GLOBAL STYLE LOCK:



Use a stylized hand-painted low-poly-inspired 2D game asset style.



The rendering must remain consistent with the reference asset pack:

clean readable silhouette,

chunky simplified geometry,

clear polygonal planes,

restrained detail density,

flat matte material presentation,

and polished game-ready asset presentation.



Do not render the asset as realistic concept art.



LIGHTING AND SHADING:



No cinematic lighting.

No realistic sunlight.

No dramatic directional light.

No rim light.

No backlight.

No glow.

No bloom.

No glossy reflections.

No PBR material response.



There must be no obvious scene light source.



Use graphic faceted shading that is baked into the design.



Shading exists only to separate geometric planes and clarify form.



Use a compressed value range:



top-facing planes = slightly lighter

front-facing planes = neutral mid value

side-facing planes = slightly darker

deep creases = moderately darker



Keep all value differences restrained.



Do not make the grassy top dramatically brighter than the cliff sides.



Do not use bright white highlights.

Do not use near-black shadows.



Do not use realistic gradients across surfaces.



Each major rock plane should remain mostly flat and uniform in value.



MATERIAL STYLE:



Use matte diffuse surfaces only.



Stone should use:

muted warm gray,

dusty lavender-gray,

subdued taupe-gray,

soft neutral beige-gray accents.



Grass should use:

muted olive green,

soft natural green,

restrained yellow-green accents.



Use minimal painted variation inside each surface.



Avoid realistic rock texture.

Avoid detailed soil texture.

Avoid erosion realism.

Avoid noisy surface detail.

Avoid micro-detail.



The entire asset should feel intentionally simplified and illustrated.



SHAPE LANGUAGE:



Create a modular terrain block with a broad readable grassy top surface and simplified vertical cliff faces underneath.



The overall form should be sturdy, compact, and usable as a modular game environment piece.



Use large readable cliff planes rather than many small fractures.



Create a few secondary rock breaks and ledges.



Avoid excessive cracks.



Avoid naturalistic geological complexity.



The silhouette should remain clean and readable from a distance.



The cliff faces must use the same exact rock shading system as the Rocks and Boulders assets.



VEGETATION:



The grass layer should remain simple and controlled.



Use a broad simplified grass surface on top.



Keep the grass edge slightly irregular and stylized.



Use only a few small grass tufts around the base and edges.



Optional:

a few tiny white flowers,

used very sparingly.



Do not allow vegetation to overpower the rock structure.



Do not create dense foliage.



Do not use large areas of bright lime green.



The grass should remain part of the same muted asset-library palette.



PRESENTATION:



Single isolated modular cliff terrain asset.



3/4 slightly elevated game-asset viewpoint.



Fully visible.



Centered composition.



Warm off-white or very light neutral background.



No environment.

No landscape.

No mountains.

No sky.

No atmospheric perspective.

No scenery.



Use only a very soft pale contact shadow directly underneath the asset.



The contact shadow must remain subtle and consistent with all other assets in the library.



FINAL STYLE TARGET:



The final result should look like a modular terrain piece from the same stylized hand-painted low-poly game asset pack.



It must prioritize:

style consistency,

readable geometry,

flat material presentation,

simplified faceted forms,

restrained baked-in shading,

and compatibility with the rest of the asset library.



Different asset categories may have different geometry, but they must never use a different rendering style.

painterly realism, cinematic concept art, splash art, realistic lighting,

sunlight, golden hour, directional lighting, dramatic shadows, rim light,

backlight, bloom, glow, volumetric lighting, global illumination,

weathering detail, photographic texture, atmospheric perspective,

depth haze, environment background, landscape, sky,

highly saturated lime green, excessive moss, dense vegetation,

anime cel shading, toon outline, thick outlines, mobile game icon lighting



and for the  Rocks  the same  Negative Prompt and :  Use the provided reference image as a strict visual style guide.



Create a ROCKS AND BOULDERS CLUSTER as a single isolated game asset belonging to the same unified stylized asset library.



GLOBAL STYLE LOCK:



Use a stylized hand-painted low-poly-inspired 2D game asset style.

clear polygonal planes,

flat matte material presentation,

and polished game-ready asset presentation.



Do not render the asset as realistic concept art.



LIGHTING AND SHADING:

No realistic sunlight.

No dramatic directional light.

No rim light.

No backlight.

No glow.

No bloom.

No glossy reflections.

No PBR material response.



There must be no obvious scene light source.



Use graphic faceted shading that is baked into the design.



Shading exists only to separate geometric planes and clarify form.



Use a compressed value range:



top-facing planes = slightly lighter

front-facing planes = neutral mid value

side-facing planes = slightly darker

deep creases = moderately darker



Keep all value differences restrained.



Do not use bright white highlights.

Do not use near-black shadows.



Do not use realistic gradients across rock surfaces.



Each major rock plane should remain mostly flat and uniform in value.



MATERIAL STYLE:



Use matte diffuse surfaces only.



Stone should use:

muted warm gray,

dusty lavender-gray,

subdued taupe-gray,

soft neutral beige-gray accents.



Use minimal painted variation inside each plane.



Avoid realistic stone grain.

Avoid erosion detail.

Avoid geological realism.

Avoid noisy texture.

Avoid micro-detail.



The stone should feel intentionally simplified and illustrated.



SHAPE LANGUAGE:



Create a compact cluster of stylized boulders.



Use squat, sturdy, irregular rock shapes.



Use one or two dominant large boulders,

several medium supporting rocks,

and only a few small stones.



Avoid tall cliff-like formations.



Use softened angular corners and readable polygonal facets.



The silhouette should remain simple and recognizable at small scale.



VEGETATION:



Vegetation must remain secondary to the rocks.



Use only a few small muted-green grass tufts around the base.



Use very limited moss.



Keep approximately 85 to 90 percent of the visible rock surface clean stone.



Use muted olive green and natural medium green.



Avoid saturated lime green.



Do not cover large areas with moss.



PRESENTATION:

3/4 slightly elevated game-asset viewpoint.



Fully visible.



Centered composition.

comments.author: OriginlessGamer
comments.body:
I dunno, looks solid and consistent, what's the use case? 

do you plan to just sprinkle them across the map for your game or maybe sell as asset packs, etc.?

replies.author: Accomplished-Cat5451
replies.body: I try to use them for  a Level  of mine  , will be a 2.5D Game , I model a lot of stuff my self but i try to automate some of the Assets  cause it is to much alone

replies.author: OriginlessGamer
replies.body: The only blocker I can see is that if you try to stitch them together as tiles, they might not tile well, but if you just put them as individual things on the map, they'll look fine

replies.author: Accomplished-Cat5451
replies.body: Yes i have , but  i dont want to do a pixelart game and  character animations arent that great ,  way to much manual correction needed

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: I think this is just the state of the technology, it produces interesting results, but they are not consistent, and the model breaks when we try to generate something out of the constrains it was trained. Needs to wait for the models to improve, maybe 1 year.

replies.author: Accomplished-Cat5451
replies.body:
Yeah that’s sad , it would definitely make it easier to create less slop .   
I mean I use Ai mainly as a tool and automate task that are repetitive but in certain areas I am faster doing it myself .
